walkthroughs.body_html:
Coastal Landscapes / Glaciated Landscapes / Dryland Landscapes — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coastal Landscapes / Glaciated Landscapes / Dryland Landscapes brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coastal Landscapes / Glaciated Landscapes / Dryland Landscapes.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What changed between the MDGs (Millennium Development Goals) and the SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals)?
options: The SDGs replaced the MDGs because the MDGs were achieved.
MDGs (2000-2015) targeted LICs on basic poverty/health/education; SDGs (2015-2030) apply to all countries and include environmental and inequality goals — broader, more universal scope.
MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
Ocean acidification is caused by acid rain falling on the sea.
A drainage basin is the underground source of a river.
Ocean acidification is caused by acid rain falling on the sea.
A drainage basin is the bowl-shaped area at the mouth of the river.
The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries, bounded by a watershed (high ground that separates one basin from another).

mcqs.q: Why is ocean acidification a separate threat from ocean warming?
options: Ocean acidification is just another name for ocean warming.
Ocean acidification is caused by acid rain falling on the sea.
MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
Acidification occurs because oceans absorb atmospheric CO2, forming carbonic acid and lowering pH — this dissolves calcium carbonate shells and corals, independent of any warming.
